title: Settings
sub: Versions, quality, online services, indexers, download clients, folders, automation, media servers, notifications, tags, import and system.

versions.title: Versions
versions.intro: A version is one edition of the same title, for example Full HD and 4K. Every movie version gets a profile that says which releases fit and which are better.
versions.label: Name
versions.labelHint: For example Full HD or 4K. Each name exists only once per type.
versions.missingLabel: Please give the version a name.

remove.title: Remove version?
remove.text: The version {{label}} disappears from nexcrate. This only works while no title and no Radarr connection uses it.

clients.title: Download clients
clients.intro: The programs that download for nexcrate: SABnzbd and NZBGet for Usenet, qBittorrent, Transmission and Deluge for torrents. nexcrate fetches the file from the indexer itself and hands it over, so no client ever sees an indexer key.
clients.fromRadarr: Fetch from Radarr, Sonarr or Lidarr
clients.empty: No download client yet. Without one nexcrate cannot download anything.
clients.authPaused: nexcrate only asks qBittorrent again once you save the client or test the connection. Otherwise qBittorrent blocks nexcrate's address after five failed attempts.

kind.label: Program
kind.qbittorrentFiling: Torrents keep seeding. That is why nexcrate gives the movie a second name for the same file in the movie folder. When downloads and media are not in the same mounted folder, nexcrate copies the movie.

details.retentionUnknown: Could not be read, so nexcrate sets no limit

lastError.label: Last error: {{text}}
lastError.client_auth_failed: The client did not accept the credentials.
lastError.client_wrong_kind: A different program answers at this address.
lastError.client_category_failed: The category could not be created.
lastError.client_category_unusable: The category is set up in a way that nexcrate cannot reliably find the files.
lastError.client_host_refused: SABnzbd refuses the host name nexcrate uses to reach it. Add it in SABnzbd under Config, Special to host_whitelist, or use the IP address.
lastError.client_address_refused: The client refuses nexcrate's address. Add it to rpc-whitelist in Transmission or switch the list off.

actions.removeBlocked: Removing works once no download of {{name}} is running any more.

test.categoryMissing: The category {{category}} does not exist there yet. nexcrate creates it when you save.
test.categoryGone: The category {{category}} is missing there. Save the client once more, then nexcrate creates it again.

form.fromRadarrIntro: Address and settings come from {{source}}. Radarr does not hand out keys and passwords, you type them yourself.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Anything you like, for example SABnzbd.
form.urlHintSabnzbd: The address where you open SABnzbd in the browser, with port, for example http://sabnzbd.example.com:8080.
form.urlHintQbittorrent: The address where you open qBittorrent in the browser, with port, for example http://qbittorrent.example.com:8080.
form.apiKeyHint: You find it in SABnzbd under Config, General. Take the API key, not the NZB key.
form.passwordHint: As when you log in to the web interface of qBittorrent.
form.secretSaved: Saved. Leave the field empty to keep it.
form.categoryHint: nexcrate creates this category if it does not exist yet. It is written in lower case, the way SABnzbd keeps categories. With a category of its own, a Radarr that still runs never takes nexcrate's downloads.
form.categoryFromRadarr: Radarr uses the category {{category}}. nexcrate deliberately takes its own, otherwise Radarr would take over every download.
form.priorityHint: 1 to 50. With several clients for Usenet or for torrents, nexcrate asks the one with the lowest number first.
form.enabledHint: When switched off the client gets no new downloads.
form.saveHint: When you save, nexcrate tests the connection and creates the category.
form.categoryInvalid: The category has 1 to 64 characters: lower-case letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen.
form.priorityInvalid: The priority is a whole number from 1 to 50.
form.urlHintNzbget: The address you open NZBGet at in the browser, with the port, such as http://nzbget.example.com:6789.
form.passwordHintNzbget: User and password are in NZBGet under Settings, Security (ControlUsername, ControlPassword).
form.categoryHintNzbget: NZBGet takes any category and files downloads below its destination folder under that name; nexcrate adds nothing there. With a category of its own, a Radarr that still runs takes no downloads away from nexcrate.
form.saveHintConnectionOnly: When saving, nexcrate checks the connection.
form.urlHintTransmission: The address you open Transmission at in the browser, with the port, such as http://transmission.example.com:9091.
form.passwordHintTransmission: User and password of Transmission's web interface. Without a login, leave both empty.
form.categoryHintTransmission: Transmission puts downloads into a subfolder with this name and, from version 4 on, gives them the label too. nexcrate creates nothing there.
form.urlHintDeluge: The address you open Deluge's web interface at, with the port, such as http://deluge.example.com:8112.
form.passwordHintDeluge: The password of Deluge's web interface. It has no user name.
form.categoryHintDeluge: Deluge keeps categories as labels. nexcrate switches on the Label plugin that comes with it and adds the label when it is missing.

remove.title: Remove download client?
remove.text: {{name}} disappears from nexcrate. Nothing changes in the client itself, the category stays too.

radarr.title: Download clients from Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr
radarr.intro: nexcrate reads the download clients of your Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr connections, taken-over ones included. Nothing changes there.
radarr.empty: This connection has no SABnzbd and no qBittorrent.

automatic.title: Automation
automatic.hint: When it is on, nexcrate regularly checks your indexers for new releases, searches on a schedule for missing movies and ones that can get better, and downloads what fits the profile. It is off at first, and while it is off, nexcrate searches and downloads no movies by itself.
automatic.savedOn: Searching and downloading movies automatically is now on.
automatic.savedOff: Searching and downloading movies automatically is now off.

indexers.title: Per indexer
indexers.intro: When nexcrate last checked for new releases, how many requests are used up today and whether automation is taking a break there.
indexers.empty: No indexer added yet. Without an indexer nexcrate searches nowhere.
indexers.limitNote: You set a daily limit of your own under Indexers, when you edit the indexer.
indexers.rssNever: Never checked for new releases yet.
indexers.rssGap: When reading {{when}}, more new releases came in than nexcrate reads at once. The planned searches find what came out in between.
indexers.requestsUsedUpUntil: Today's requests are used up. Free again {{when}}.
indexers.grabsUsedUpUntil: Today's downloads are used up. Free again {{when}}.
indexers.ownLimit_one: Your daily limit: {{value}} request. nexcrate plans the automatic searches within it.
indexers.ownLimit_other: Your daily limit: {{value}} requests. nexcrate plans the automatic searches within it.
indexers.noLimit: No daily limit known. nexcrate then searches there by itself at most every two minutes.
indexers.paused: After errors, automation takes a break here until {{when}}. Your own searches go on.

automatic.seriesHint: When it is on, nexcrate searches on a schedule for missing episodes of your own series versions and ones that can get better, from the day after they aired, and downloads new episodes as soon as your indexers have them. It is off at first, and while it is off, nexcrate searches and downloads no series by itself.
automatic.seriesSavedOn: Searching and downloading series automatically is now on.
automatic.seriesSavedOff: Searching and downloading series automatically is now off.
automatic.musicHint: With the switch on, nexcrate searches missing albums of your own music version on a plan, from the release day on, and albums below the target of your music profile, and loads new releases as soon as they appear at your indexers. Albums with missing tracks it does not search by itself. Albums Lidarr feeds never. Off from the start.
automatic.musicSavedOn: Search and load music automatically is on now.
automatic.musicSavedOff: Search and load music automatically is off now.

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.hint: nexcrate puts subtitle files from the download next to the movie.
subtitles.savedOn: nexcrate now puts subtitles next to the movie.

folders.title: Default folders
folders.intro: Every version has a default folder. nexcrate files new titles of that version there.
folders.mountsIntro: nexcrate only shows folders it can see itself. You never type a path.
folders.noMounts: nexcrate does not see a folder for media yet.
folders.composeHint: Mount your media and downloads into the container, for example under /media, and restart nexcrate. For hardlinks, downloads and media must lie in the same mounted folder.
folders.noVersions: There is no movie version yet.
folders.none: No default folder yet. Without one this version downloads nothing.
folders.hint: nexcrate files new movies of this version here. Existing movies stay in their folder.
folders.chooseBlocked: You can choose a default folder as soon as nexcrate sees a mounted folder.
folders.cleared: {{label}} has no default folder any more.
folders.hintMusic: Below it nexcrate makes a folder per artist and per album. Albums that lie elsewhere already stay there.
folders.noVersionsMusic: There is no music version yet. It comes with the music profile or the first artist.

picker.title: Default folder for {{label}}
picker.empty: There are no subfolders here. You can still take this folder.
picker.takeBlocked: Open one of the mounted folders first.

naming.title: Default naming
naming.intro: This is how nexcrate names folders and files when it files them away, unless a version has its own naming. Text in curly braces is a token and gets filled in.
naming.tokensHint: They are named as in Radarr, so patterns from there can be taken over. A click puts the token where you last were in a pattern.
naming.umlautsHint: ä becomes ae, ß becomes ss. When switched off, umlauts stay as they are.
naming.previewEmpty: A pattern is empty. nexcrate cannot build a name like that.
naming.notes: The recommendation comes from the TRaSH Guides. Existing files are not renamed, the patterns apply from the next filing away.

versionNaming.title: Naming per version
versionNaming.intro: Every movie version uses the default naming or patterns of its own, for example those of the Radarr that filled it so far. Existing files are not renamed.

radarrNaming.title: Naming from Radarr for {{label}}
radarrNaming.intro: This is how Radarr names movie folders and movie files. Once taken, it applies to the version {{label}} from the next filing away. Existing files keep their names.
radarrNaming.cannotTake: nexcrate cannot take this naming as it is. What does not fit is shown at the pattern. {{label}} keeps its naming.

notes.radarr_no_rename: Radarr does not rename files, they keep the release name. nexcrate takes that over as {Original Title}.
notes.slash_in_pattern: Radarr makes subfolders with /. nexcrate writes a + there.
notes.colon_format: Radarr replaces colons differently. nexcrate replaces them like Radarr's setting Smart.
notes.illegal_characters_kept: Radarr keeps illegal characters. nexcrate replaces them.

lidarrNaming.title: Naming from Lidarr
lidarrNaming.intro: This is how Lidarr names artist folders, album folders and files. Once taken, it applies from the next filing away. Existing files keep their names until you rename them.
lidarrNaming.cannotTake: nexcrate cannot take this naming as it is. What does not fit is shown at the pattern. The naming for music stays as it is.
lidarrNaming.taken: Lidarr's naming now applies to music.

notes.lidarr_no_rename: Lidarr does not rename files, they keep the name they came with. nexcrate takes that over as {Original Filename}.
notes.slash_in_pattern: Lidarr makes subfolders with /. nexcrate writes a + there.
notes.colon_format: Lidarr replaces colons differently. nexcrate replaces them like Lidarr's setting Smart.
notes.illegal_characters_kept: Lidarr keeps illegal characters. nexcrate replaces them.

recycle.title: Recycle folder
recycle.intro: Replaced and deleted files stay this many days in the folder .nexcrate-recycle next to the movie and series folders, then nexcrate deletes them.
recycle.invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 365.
recycle.saved_one: Replaced files now stay one day in the recycle folder.
recycle.saved_other: Replaced files now stay {{value}} days in the recycle folder.

companions.title: Companion files
companions.intro: nexcrate puts a small file release.nex next to every movie it owns. If the database is lost, nexcrate reads the movies back in with it, without guessing.
companions.hint: With every takeover and every filing, rewritten with every upgrade.
companions.off: Off: after a loss of the database you assign the movies by hand.
companions.savedOff: nexcrate no longer writes companion files.
companions.backfillHint: Filling in writes missing and outdated release.nex files.
companions.backfillOff: Filling in works once Write companion files is on.

running.hint: You can leave the page, nexcrate keeps working.

report.versions_one: One version with a file looked at.
report.versions_other: {{value}} versions with a file looked at.
report.allCurrent: Every companion file is there and current.

count.file_missing_one: One is missing its movie file.
count.folder_missing_one: One is missing its movie folder.
count.no_space_one: One without space on the disk.
count.shared_one: One album shares its folder with another; nexcrate writes none there.
count.shared_other: {{value}} albums share their folder with another; nexcrate writes none there.

companions.notWritable: nexcrate may not write there. The movies stay as they are. Give nexcrate write permission there and then fill in.
companions.replaceText: The old file goes into the recycle folder. Then nexcrate writes its release.nex into the folder.
companions.replaceStopped: The release.nex in {{folder}} was not written ({{state}}).

seriesNaming.title: Naming of series
seriesNaming.intro: How nexcrate names series folders, season folders and episode files when filing. The tokens are named as in Sonarr. Replacing umlauts holds for movies and series.
seriesNaming.additionsHint: Adds the id your server recognizes to the series folder. Each addition fits its own server only: Emby matches wrongly with Plex's, Plex merges series with Jellyfin's.
seriesNaming.numberingHint: Like TMDB fits Plex and Jellyfin by default, like TVDB fits Emby. An episode without a TVDB number is named after TMDB. Applies to files stored from now on: existing files keep their numbers, so one season can then hold both.

examples.special_numbering: Special with other numbers at TMDB and TVDB
examples.special_placeholder: Special with a placeholder name at TMDB

seriesNaming.notes: The recommendation comes from the TRaSH Guides, the series folder without an id. Existing files are not renamed; series and season folders keep the name of the first filing.
seriesNaming.saved: The naming of series is saved.
seriesNaming.versionsIntro: Each series version numbers its files like TMDB or like TVDB and can have patterns of its own.
seriesNaming.noVersions: There is no version for series yet.
seriesNaming.fromSonarrLabel: Take the naming of {{label}} from Sonarr

musicNaming.title: Naming
musicNaming.intro: How artist and album folders and the files nexcrate files are named. Flat from the start: one folder per album, the medium in the file name only with several. nexcrate does not rename existing files.
musicNaming.saved: The naming of music is saved.
musicNaming.notes: {Release Year} is the year the album first came out, not the year of the release. When two albums of an artist share a name, the folder gets an addition. Players read the order of several media from the tags, not from the name. Whoever prefers a folder per medium writes it in front of the file name of "File, several media" with a /, as Lidarr does: {Medium Format} {medium:00}/{track:00} {Track Title}. The folder needs {medium}; "Rename" tidies the albums that are there afterwards.

bin.title: In the recycle bin
bin.intro: Deleted files, by you or by a program with a key. Taking one back puts it where it was.
bin.gone: The file is gone, or its disk cannot be seen right now.
bin.notInLibrary: The title or its version is no longer in the library. It cannot go back.
bin.emptyText: Every file in the recycle bin is deleted for good right now. This cannot be undone.
bin.purgeText: The file is deleted for good right now. This cannot be undone.

rules.title: Library rules
rules.hint: The first rule that fits decides where a new title of this version goes; otherwise the default folder. Titles already there stay where they are.
rules.saved: The rules of the version {{label}} are saved.
rules.ratingsHint: The rating of the country set under Calendar, such as 0, 6 for children's films. Without a country this rule never fits.
rules.moveLabel: Move the titles of the version {{label}} by its rules
rules.moveIntro: These titles lie elsewhere than the rules say. Each moves with its whole folder, on the same disk only; a title moves whole or stays.
rules.moveNothing: Every title already lies where the rules want it.
rules.skipMissing: Stays: its folder cannot be seen.
rules.skipOtherDisk: Stays: the target is on another disk.
rules.skipShared: Stays: another version lies in the same folder.
rules.skipTaken: Stays: the folder already exists at the target.
rules.skipBusy: Stays: the title is being filed or renamed right now.

services.title: Other services
services.intro: Services on the internet that nexcrate asks. Each can be switched off; what is missing then is said below it. No file ever leaves.

rename.title: Rename existing files

intro.movie: Renames movie folders and files by the naming of their version. Subtitles follow, and so do other files in the folder.
intro.series: Renames series, season and specials folders and every episode by the naming of their version. Unclear files keep their place in the series folder.
intro.music: Renames artist and album folders and every track by the music naming. Albums sharing a folder get one each. Tags stay as they are.

rename.notComputed: No preview yet. Computing only reads and changes nothing.
rename.nothing: Everything is named as the naming wants it already.

unit.left_one: {{count}} file stays in the old folder, because music of other albums lies there too.
unit.left_other: {{count}} files stay in the old folder, because music of other albums lies there too.

skip.folder_missing: The folder cannot be seen, for example because the disk is missing.
skip.file_missing: A file is missing on disk.
skip.busy: Downloading or being filed right now. The next run takes it.
skip.link: A link is in the way. nexcrate follows no links.
skip.target_taken: Target taken: “{{name}}” exists already. It stays as it is.
skip.target_twice: Two files would get the same name “{{name}}”.
skip.target_planned: Another title would get the same target “{{name}}”.
skip.several_roots: The albums lie in several root folders.
skip.file_twice: A file belongs to two albums.
skip.move_failed: A file could not be moved. Everything is back.
skip.database: The database refused the rename. Everything is back.
skip.changed: The title changed since the run.
skip.files_moved: The files are no longer where the run put them.

note.folder_shared: Another title lies in the folder. The folder keeps its name; only the files in it are renamed.
note.artist_folder_shared: Albums of other artists lie in the artist folder. It keeps its name.
note.folder_split: This album shared a folder with other albums and gets its own. What belongs to no album stays in the old folder.
note.facts_missing: For at least one file nexcrate knows neither the release name nor media data. Codec, HDR, audio and custom formats are missing from the new name.

last.title: Last run
last.undoHint: Works as long as nothing was filed or changed for these titles since the run. Such titles stay as they are.

confirm.title: Rename?
confirm.text: {{units}} with {{files}} files and {{folders}} folders in all are renamed.
confirm.players: Plex and other players see the files under new names and read them again at their next scan. Files are only renamed and moved within their root folder, never copied and never overwritten.

running.title: Renaming
running.done: Done: {{done}} renamed with {{files}} files and {{folders}} folders, {{skipped}} left out, {{failed}} failed.
running.undone: Done: {{undone}} taken back, {{kept}} stay as they are.
running.failed: The job stopped. What was done stays; titles in the middle are back.

titleButton.label: Rename: {{name}}
titleButton.title: Rename {{name}}
titleButton.intro: This is how nexcrate would name folders and files by the naming of the version.
titleButton.introAlbum: This is how nexcrate would name the album folder and tracks. The artist folder stays, as not the whole artist is renamed.
titleButton.nothing: Nothing to rename here: folders and files are named as the naming wants it already.

delay.intro: Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr call this a delay profile. It sets which protocol wins between releases that are otherwise equal, and how long the automatic waits to see whether a better release turns up. From the factory it is the same as there: Usenet wins, nothing waits.
delay.preferredHint: Decides only between releases of the same quality and score. A better release always wins, wherever it comes from.
delay.waitHint: Counted from when the indexer published the release. 0 means load at once.
delay.offHint: A protocol that is switched off does not fit this version. By hand such a release loads only with a confirmation.
delay.exceptionsIdle: They only apply once a waiting time is entered.
delay.bypassQuality: Load the best quality at once
delay.bypassQualityHint: A release in the best quality the profile allows does not wait. Applies to {{protocol}} only, the preferred protocol.
delay.bypassScore: Load at once from a certain score
delay.bypassScoreHint: A release whose custom format score reaches the threshold does not wait. Applies to {{protocol}} only.
delay.manualNote: Only the automatic waits. Whoever presses Load or Search automatically now gets the release at once. What waits is listed under Downloads, tab Waiting.

read.label: Read from a connection
read.hint: Reads the delay profiles and fills them in here, those with tags below in their order. Nothing is stored before you press Save.
read.done: Read. Check the values and save.
read.nothing: There is no delay profile without a tag there that can be used here.
read.tagged_one: {{count}} profile with tags could not be used, for instance because both protocols are off.
read.tagged_other: {{count}} profiles with tags could not be used, for instance because both protocols are off.
read.shortened: A waiting time of more than 30 days was cut down to 30 days.
read.taggedCame_one: {{count}} profile with tags came along, below under “Different for titles with tags”.
read.taggedCame_other: {{count}} profiles with tags came along, below under “Different for titles with tags”.

problem.minutes: The waiting time is a whole number from 0 to 43200 minutes (30 days).
problem.score: The threshold is a whole number.
problem.bothOff: At least one protocol has to stay on, or the version could never load anything.
problem.tags: Every rule for tags needs at least one tag.

tagged.title: Different for titles with tags
tagged.hint: Like the delay profiles with tags in Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr. When a title carries one of a rule's tags, the first fitting rule from the top holds; otherwise the rule above. A new rule takes the exceptions from above.
tagged.tagsHint: Several separated by commas. A tag that does not exist yet is created.

delay.taggedCount_one: Plus {{count}} rule for titles with tags.
delay.taggedCount_other: Plus {{count}} rules for titles with tags.

servers.title: Media servers
servers.intro: nexcrate tells Plex, Jellyfin and Emby when a folder has changed: after every filed download and after renaming. A new movie then shows up in the player within a minute or two instead of after the server's next scan. A media server that does not answer never holds up an import.
servers.empty: No media server connected yet. New files then appear only when the server looks by itself.

lastError.label: Last error: {{text}}
lastError.mediaserver_auth_failed: The server did not accept the token or API key.
lastError.mediaserver_wrong_kind: Another program answers at the address.
lastError.mediaserver_http_error: The server answered with an error.

servers.unmatched: The last folder lay in no library of this server. nexcrate guessed nothing and had the whole library read again instead. Does the server see the folders under another path than nexcrate? Then a path mapping is missing.

notify.folder: Last told {{when}}: the changed folder only.
notify.library: Last told {{when}}: whole library read again.

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.hint: Only libraries that are switched on hear about changes.
libraries.none: The server named no libraries. Check the connection again.

mappings.title: Path mapping
mappings.intro: Only needed when the server sees the same folders under another path than nexcrate, such as /media here and /volume1/media there.
mappings.suggested: Suggested from the folders the server lists and the folders of your versions. Please check; nothing is stored before you press Save.
mappings.notNeeded: No mapping needed: the server sees the folders of your versions under the same path.
mappings.incomplete: Every path mapping needs both sides.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Anything you like, such as Plex living room.
form.urlHintPlex: The address of your Plex with its port, such as http://plex.example.com:32400.
form.urlHintJellyfin: The address you open Jellyfin at in the browser, such as http://jellyfin.example.com:8096.
form.urlHintEmby: The address you open Emby at in the browser, such as http://emby.example.com:8096.
form.tokenHint: The X-Plex-Token of your server. Typed in here, plex.tv is not needed: nexcrate then talks to your server only.
form.apiKeyHintJellyfin: In Jellyfin under Dashboard, API Keys.
form.apiKeyHintEmby: In Emby under Settings, API Keys.
form.secretSaved: Saved. Leave the field empty to keep it.
form.enabledHint: Switched off, the server hears nothing from nexcrate.
form.saveHint: Saving tests the connection and reads the libraries. Nothing changes on the server.

plexTv.title: Sign-in
plexTv.intro: Sign in at plex.tv and pick your server: address, name and token then come by themselves. Or enter address and token by hand below. nexcrate talks to plex.tv only when you press the button.
plexTv.open: Open the sign-in page of plex.tv
plexTv.waiting: Confirm the sign-in on the page of plex.tv. nexcrate keeps asking plex.tv until then.
plexTv.claimed: Signed in. nexcrate takes the token when you save; it never leaves nexcrate's server.
plexTv.expired: The sign-in has expired. Start it again.

servers.none: plex.tv lists no server of its own for this account. Enter the address by hand below; the token of the sign-in still holds.
servers.sharedHidden_one: {{count}} server is only shared with you and is therefore not offered.
servers.sharedHidden_other: {{count}} servers are only shared with you and are therefore not offered.
servers.choosing: Looking for the server at its addresses, the local ones first.
servers.chosen: {{name}} answers at {{url}}. Address and token are filled in.

remove.title: Remove media server?
remove.text: {{name}} disappears from nexcrate, with its stored access. Nothing changes on the server itself.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.intro: Ratings of IMDb for the library, a title's page and other programs; with an OMDb key of your own also Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic.
ratings.imdbSwitch: Load IMDb's ratings once a day
ratings.imdbHint: nexcrate fetches IMDb's file itself, for personal and non-commercial use only. Switched off, nexcrate never asks IMDb.
ratings.problem: The last load failed; the loaded values stay.
ratings.omdbIntro: With a key of your own from omdbapi.com (1,000 requests a day for free). nexcrate keeps every answer 30 days. Series have no such values there.
ratings.omdbHasKey: A key is stored. Today {{today}} of {{limit}} requests.

tagField.indexerHint: With tags nexcrate asks this indexer only for titles with one of them, as Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr do. Without tags it serves every title.
tagField.clientHint: With tags this client loads only titles with one of them, and such titles load only through clients with a fitting tag when there is one. Without tags it loads everything else.

upgrades.title: Hold back upgrades
upgrades.intro: nexcrate always searches and loads what is missing. Here you only hold back the automatic upgrades of what is there. Nothing holds back what you load yourself.
upgrades.pauseHint: Nothing that is there when you switch this on is upgraded automatically any more. What arrives afterwards is upgraded as usual. Switching it off lifts the pause for everything.
upgrades.pausedSince: Paused since {{date}}. What arrived since is still upgraded.
upgrades.pausedOn: Upgrades of what is there are paused.
upgrades.perDay: At most this many upgrades a day
upgrades.perDayHint: Automatic upgrade downloads in 24 hours. 0 means no limit.
upgrades.perDaySavedNone: Upgrades have no daily limit any more.
upgrades.used_one: In the last 24 hours: {{value}} automatic upgrade.
upgrades.used_other: In the last 24 hours: {{value}} automatic upgrades.
upgrades.usedOf: In the last 24 hours: {{used}} of {{limit}} automatic upgrades.
